title: quant-tradeoff-slackline-calculator-notes
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, reproducible spreadsheet-style calculator and guidance for evaluating INT8, FP8 and 4-bit (low-bit) quantization options against three operational axes: per-token cost, latency (p99 and avg), and quality (task-specific metric delta). This doc captures the assumptions and the column layout we actually use in a working Google Sheet prototype (separate artifact).

High-level approach (slackline metaphor):
- Treat quantization choice as balancing on a slackline between cost at the left and quality at the right; latency is the wind that shifts the center and changes the required balance.
- Start from measured baseline (FP16 or FP32) on representative hardware and a sampled prompt set for the target workload.
- Produce normalized multipliers for cost and latency for each quant variant and an empirical quality delta per metric.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline = FP16 serving profile with current kernel set on A100/MI300-like hardware. If customer baseline is different, normalize to their baseline first.
- Cost = raw GPU time * per-GPU-minute $ + infra overhead (per-request fixed overhead). We provide a per-token cost normalization factor rather than absolute dollars initially so the sheet is portable.
- Latency = end-to-end server-side p50/p95/p99 including batching overhead and KV cache hit ratio.
- Quality = measured on the customer's evaluation prompts; for classification use accuracy/F1, for summarization use ROUGE-1/2-L or human judgement proxy. We report absolute delta and percent relative change.

Inputs required (sheet columns):
- model_name (string): e.g., llama-3-13b, redwood-alpha-7b
- baseline_fp (string): FP16/FP32 baseline label
- seq_len (int): typical request token length (mean)
- prompt_frac_cache_hit (float 0-1): estimated prefix/KV cache hit rate
- q_variant (string): int8, fp8, 4bit, int8+kv, etc.
- tokens_per_request (int): mean output tokens (for per-token cost)
- baseline_gpu_token_throughput (float): tokens/sec baseline measured
- quant_gpu_throughput (float): tokens/sec measured for quantized variant
- infra_overhead_ms (float): fixed overhead per request (ms) for orchestration
- price_per_gpu_min_usd (float): cost of one GPU-minute for the target tier
- quality_metric_baseline (float): metric value on eval set for baseline
- quality_metric_quant (float): metric value on eval set for quantized model
- calibration_sample_size (int): number of eval samples used

Derived/Output columns (calculated by sheet formulas):
- throughput_ratio = quant_gpu_throughput / baseline_gpu_token_throughput
- latency_ms_baseline = (tokens_per_request / baseline_gpu_token_throughput)*1000 + infra_overhead_ms*(1 - prompt_frac_cache_hit)
- latency_ms_quant = (tokens_per_request / quant_gpu_throughput)*1000 + infra_overhead_ms*(1 - prompt_frac_cache_hit)
- latency_delta_ms = latency_ms_quant - latency_ms_baseline
- cost_per_token_baseline_usd = (1/ baseline_gpu_token_throughput) * (price_per_gpu_min_usd / 60)
- cost_per_token_quant_usd = (1/ quant_gpu_throughput) * (price_per_gpu_min_usd / 60) * (1 - amortized_cache_savings)
- cost_multiplier = cost_per_token_quant_usd / cost_per_token_baseline_usd
- quality_delta_abs = quality_metric_quant - quality_metric_baseline
- quality_delta_pct = quality_delta_abs / max(0.0001, quality_metric_baseline)
- decision_score (heuristic) = w_cost*(1 - cost_multiplier) + w_latency*( - latency_delta_ms/100) + w_quality*( - quality_delta_pct*100)

Notes on specific fields and quick formulas: 
- amortized_cache_savings: user-specified estimate (0-0.5). Low-bit KV caching may have different effects; default 0.1 for initial sims.
- throughput measurements should be measured with continuous batching similar to production traffic shape (use 95th percentile batch size distribution).
- price_per_gpu_min_usd should include effective discounts (committed reserved capacity) if applicable.

Example numeric knobs (for quick simulation):
- Example baseline throughput (13B FP16): 12k tokens/s
- Example INT8 throughput: 18k tokens/s (throughput_ratio = 1.5)
- Example FP8 throughput: 15k tokens/s (ratio = 1.25)
- Example 4-bit throughput: 28k tokens/s (ratio = 2.33)
- price_per_gpu_min_usd: $3.50 (placeholder for a mid-tier GPU)
- tokens_per_request: 60 (avg chat turn)
- infra_overhead_ms: 12 ms
- prompt_frac_cache_hit: 0.35
- quality_metric_baseline (e.g., summarization ROUGE-L): 0.42
- quality_metric_4bit: 0.395 (quality_delta_abs = -0.025 ~ -6% relative)

Quick worked example row (numbers derived from above):
- latency_ms_baseline = (60 / 12000)*1000 + 12*(1-0.35) = 5ms + 7.8ms = 12.8ms
- latency_ms_4bit = (60 / 28000)*1000 + 12*(1-0.35) = 2.14ms + 7.8ms = 9.94ms (delta = -2.86ms)
- cost_per_token_baseline = (1/12000) * (3.5/60) = 0.000004861 USD/token
- cost_per_token_4bit = (1/28000) * (3.5/60) = 0.000002084 USD/token
- cost_multiplier ~ 0.429 (i.e., ~57% savings)
- quality_delta_pct ~ (0.395 - 0.42)/0.42 = -0.0595 (~ -6%)

Heuristic decision guidance (proposed):
- If quality_delta_pct >= -1% (i.e., <=1% degradation) -> accept quant variant if cost_multiplier <= 0.85 (>=15% savings).
- If quality_delta_pct between -1% and -5% -> accept only if latency delta is negative (latency improved) and cost_multiplier <= 0.60 (>=40% savings) OR if business prioritizes cost over quality for this workload (flag in sheet).
- If quality_delta_pct < -5% -> do not deploy without targeted finetune/post-calibration unless cost savings > 70% and this is a non-customer-facing batch task.

Edge cases and caveats:
- Small sample sizes can make quality deltas noisy. Add Wilson score or bootstrap CI columns when calibration_sample_size < 500.
- For generation tasks, automatic metrics can be misleading. Add human eval checklist column when quality_delta_pct is close to thresholds.
- Some kernels for int8/4bit behave poorly with long kv-cache lengths; test both short and long context profiles.
- Mixed-mode (kv in int8, attn in fp8) can yield non-linear interactions; the sheet allows multi-mode rows and aggregated effective throughput.

Recommended spreadsheet layout tabs (sheet names):
- README (this doc condensed)
- RawMeasurements (one row per experiment run with flags)
- NormalizedSummary (per model+variant aggregated averages and stdev)
- Scenarios (scenario builder grid to sweep prompt lengths, cache_hit, price)
- DecisionMatrix (outputs: recommended variant and rationale text for each scenario)
- AuditLog (linked artifacts, run ids, PRs, timestamps)

Open questions / next actions:
- Decide default weights for decision_score (w_cost, w_latency, w_quality). Proposal: w_quality=0.6, w_latency=0.2, w_cost=0.2 for customer-facing tasks; swap to w_cost=0.5 for batch-only internal workloads.
- Integrate with Redwood Console telemetry to pull real traffic batch-size distribution and p95 cache hit rate automatically into Scenarios tab.
- Add a small script to convert the sheet rows into perf test harness configs (Jenkins/GHA job) for automated A/B runs.

Todo (short list):
- [ ] Create the Google Sheet from the layout above and populate with three baseline + quant runs for two models (13B, 70B). Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-02-28.
- [ ] Add bootstrap CI column and a human-eval checklist entry for generation tasks. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-03-05.
- [ ] Link runs to PR that added optimized int8 kernel for the 13B model. Owner: Lucas. JIRA:OPT-412.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- keep a short hand column for "conviction" (low/medium/high) to capture whether metric signals are robust.
- call out any runs where the quantized model diverged or produced collapsed outputs — these are catastrophic and should gate deployment regardless of cost.

Appendix: quick sanity-check thresholds we use in playbooks for rollouts:
- Canary: start on 0.5-1% traffic, monitor perplexity/latency/cost per token with automatic rollback on >2% absolute metric drop or +10% p99 latency.
- Gradual ramp: 1 -> 5 -> 20% with 24h between steps and human review on metric drift.

If you want, I can spin up the starter Google Sheet and push a CSV with the example numbers above (separate artifact).
